 B OISE — A text message from a Boise State legend turned a difficult travel day into a memorable one for Bronco quarterback Maddux Madsen.
 Madsen was on the team bus, watching some TV on the way from Portland to Eugene after the Broncos’ flight prior to their season opener at Oregon in September. All of a sudden, his phone lit up with a message from Kellen Moore, the former Boise State quarterback who went 50-3 in four years as a starter. Madsen said he had never really interacted with Moore before, but the message told him good luck on the upcoming season and to not hesitate reaching out if he needed anything from him.
 “I saw my parents at the hotel at family time, I told my dad and my dad’s like ‘no way,’ Madsen remembers. “He was just as excited as I was.”
 Madsen said he has not been in communication with Moore since, but all that might change this week. Moore, who is currently the head coach of the New Orleans Saints, will be back in town Saturday night as the Broncos (6-1, 3-0 Pac-12) take on Texas State (4-3, 2-1). At halftime, a statue in Moore’s likeness will be unveiled on the field at Albertsons Stadium before it heads to its permanent home outside the Broncos’ recruiting lounge on the northeast side of the stadium.
 Boise sculptor Benjamin Victor poses with a clay model of the Kellen Moore statue he is sculpting, which will be unveiled at halftime of Boise State’s game against Texas State on Saturday.
 Boise State Athletics Photo 
 With the Saints on the bye week, Moore is able to take the time to return to Boise for the honor. He will also raise the blue chaos flag prior to kickoff.
 “I’m just excited for our guys to see him in person,” said Boise State coach Spencer Danielson.
 “There’s a lot of pictures around our building, rightfully so, of Kellen Moore. When you go 50-3, every bit is earned. So, I’m excited for our guys to be able to see him.”
 Almost 15 years after he played his final game on The Blue, it’s hard to overstate the impact that Moore left in Boise. If you were to build a Mount Rushmore of Bronco greats, it would be practically universally accepted that it would be incomplete without him. Simply put, a lot of what Boise State has today can be traced back to Moore.
 In addition to being college football’s winningest quarterback, the Broncos never had more than one loss in any of the four seasons he was their starting quarterback. In his sophomore year, Boise State went 14-0, including a win over TCU in the Fiesta Bowl. The following season, Moore had Boise State ranked as high as No. 2 in the Associated Press Top 25 and the Broncos were in the BCS championship conversation until a late-season loss to Nevada. That season, Moore also became Boise State’s first Heisman Trophy finalist, finishing fourth.
 Boise State’s Kellen Moore passes in the first half of the Broncos’ 42-7 home victory over Hawaii on Nov. 6, 2010 in Boise.
 Idaho Press File Photo 
 “I’m joking that he deserves a statue on every corner of campus,” said Boise State offensive coordinator Nate Potter, who blocked for Moore as an offensive tackle while the two were teammates at Boise State. “It’s part of the reason why we have all of these new buildings. But he deserves everything and it’s cool that it’s finally coming to fruition, they’re going to commemorate him. He’s a great example of a football player, but also a human being.”
 Boise State announced the statue on June 30, during the Broncos’ celebration of officially joining the Pac-12. The 11-foot bronze statue, which will depict Moore in his signature passing pose, was sculpted by local artist Benjamin Victor, who also sculpted the statue of former Boise State coach Lyle Smith, which sits outside the Allen Noble Hall of Fame on Albertsons Stadium’s southwest side.
 In addition to the Statue, Moore was honored on the new Blue Turf installed this summer at Albertsons Stadium with the 11-yard hash marks at both ends of the field being painted orange, in honor of the No. 11 he wore at Boise State. The 2-yard hash marks were also painted orange in honor of running back Ashton Jeanty, who was the 2024 Heisman Trophy runner-up.
 “I don’t think that anyone can argue that there’s not one person more deserving,” Madsen said of Moore. “Obviously, what he’s done for this program, it’s still talked about to this day. He’s exceptional for Boise State football, especially as a quarterback, that’s something you’re always trying to chase. Obviously that legacy is very challenging to chase, but you get to chase it here.”
